freshness_notes.tfl_webcat: official TfL planning connectivity toolkit checked July 2026; PTAL and TIM support current/base and future network scenarios and are strategic planning tools
freshness_notes.dft_road_traffic: 2025 traffic data published 20 May 2026; London has 3,665 count points; count-vs-estimated quality flags preserved
freshness_notes.gias: official school register supports search/download and daily public data updates; system updated 21 July 2026
freshness_notes.school_capacity: 2024/25 release published 19 March 2026; school-level capacity and planned-place datasets available
freshness_notes.nhs_ods: live national organisation/site reference service; core search/export and APIs update overnight/daily; service pages updated April-May 2026
freshness_notes.lgif: London Green Infrastructure Framework first published January 2026; corrected London-wide data version 1 April 2026
freshness_notes.cultural_infrastructure: 2026 GLA cultural infrastructure production data published May-June 2026
freshness_notes.heat_networks: London Assembly analysis published 2 March 2026 using GLA London Heat Map accessed January 2026

query_preparation.promotion_rule: Source/search/API/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains PENDING_RAW_RESPONSE until a candidate-specific response/record is captured and provenance can be hashed.

batches.c: PTAL combines walking access to public transport with service wait time. Candidate use requires the exact WebCAT location/cell; it is strategic connectivity, not a guaranteed journey time.
WebCAT can show future transport-network scenarios. Future PTAL must not be treated as current accessibility until the relevant network change is delivered.
TIM creates travel-time catchments for a selected location, year, mode, period and direction. Exact candidate input and scenario parameters are required.

batches.t: Unified API StopPoint proximity query prep
batches.c: TfL Unified API exposes StopPoint data in consistent JSON structures. Nearby stops require exact coordinate query/result capture; stop proximity alone does not prove service quality.
TfL Places capability supports location lookup and matching. Candidate promotion requires exact resolved place/postcode or coordinate relation rather than name-only matching.
Route and line topology can support candidate network context, but current service patterns and disruptions must be distinguished from static topology.
DfT publishes geolocated traffic count points. Candidate use requires an exact nearest/link relation and the count point's road/link identity.
The current road-traffic site uses data published 20 May 2026 for 2025. AADF is a modelled annual average and must retain year and method flags.
DfT marks count methods; counted estimates are generally more reliable than estimated ones. Candidate evidence must preserve estimation_method and detailed method.
Cars, LGVs, HGVs, buses, motorcycles and cycles have different development implications. Exact link/count-point relation is required before using class flows.
Raw observations and annual average estimates are different evidence types. A single raw count must not be promoted as annual traffic exposure.
DfT warns individual road-link and small-area estimates can be less robust than regional statistics. Site-level conclusions remain fail-closed without stronger local evidence where available.
GIAS is the official register of schools and colleges and supports location search/download. Exact establishment/URN and status are required for candidate proximity.
DfE school-capacity data provide school places and pupils on roll. Exact school URN linkage is required; GIAS presence alone does not establish spare capacity.
Unfilled places are reported in the capacity release. They are a time-specific capacity indicator and not a guaranteed admission place for a future development.
DfE records pupils in schools above stated capacity. Candidate use requires exact school/planning-area linkage and current-year context.
DfE publishes planned capacity changes with firm delivery plans for future years. Planned places are future supply, not current spare capacity.
SCAP includes pupil forecasts and planned changes. Area demand supports infrastructure planning but does not itself establish a developer contribution or site capacity.
ODS provides unique codes, addresses and status for health organisations. Exact ODS organisation/site and address relation are required; proximity does not prove appointment capacity.
ODS covers pharmacies and maintains organisation status/address data. Candidate use requires exact active organisation and location matching.
ODS contains trusts and sites with unique identifiers. Organisation identity must be separated from individual service availability or capacity.
ODS publishes open/close dates, status and last-change information. Closed or superseded organisations must not be counted as current access.
Core ODS search/export and APIs are refreshed overnight/daily. Candidate evidence should retain retrieval date and organisation last-change state.
NHS service search can crosscheck publicly discoverable hospitals/pharmacies. It remains a service-location check, not a capacity or waiting-time assessment.
GLA Cultural Infrastructure Map locates cultural facilities and can be viewed with transport/population context. Snapshot status and facility type must be preserved.
The 2025/26 GLA dataset includes production data supplied in May-June 2026. It is a snapshot and missing facilities are not negative proof.
LGIF, first published January 2026, brings London-wide green-infrastructure data together. Candidate conclusions require exact spatial indicators rather than borough averages.
GLA notes early CSV errors were corrected in the 1 April 2026 version. Superseded files must not be used for current candidate evidence.
GLA Green Cover 2024 is available as geospatial tiles in EPSG:27700. Exact candidate/tile geometry is required; borough percentages are context only.
Remote-sensing/land-use modelling estimates green cover. It is not a surveyed parcel landscape plan and must not be converted directly into scheme-level UGF or BNG outcomes.
IMA maps growth, development and infrastructure investment. Exact project geometry/status/date is required before associating a candidate with an infrastructure benefit or disruption.
Future infrastructure investment shown in IMA is planned/forecast evidence. It must not be treated as delivered capacity before operational status is confirmed.
IMA can model likelihood of residential projects delivering by a date. A model probability is not a planning permission or completion record for the candidate.
GLA High Street boundaries support exact spatial context for community/commercial areas. Boundary membership is context, not proof of footfall, spend or retail viability.
Town-centre boundaries identify concentrations of commercial, cultural and civic activity. Exact boundary relation and current planning policy remain required.

batches.t: High Streets Data Service coverage-limit gate
batches.c: HSDS provides members with spend, footfall and vacancy data while open data includes boundaries. Proprietary/member-only indicators are not inferred when not directly available.
The GLA air-quality map shows monitoring stations and mobile-sensor coverage. Nearby monitoring does not equal parcel concentration without exact model/monitor relation.
The map includes historical/projected NO2 layers and policy actions. Projected 2025 surfaces are model outputs and must not be presented as measured 2026 parcel values.
Borough monitoring, diffusion tubes and mobile sensors have different methods. Candidate evidence must preserve source type, period and spatial representativeness.
Heat-map evidence can identify existing heat networks and sources. Exact candidate/network relation and connection feasibility are required before treating it as usable capacity.
Proposed heat networks are future infrastructure and must remain separate from existing networks; planned proximity is not an available connection.
NHS pharmacy search supports nearby service discovery. Exact location and current service record are required, and proximity does not establish opening hours or service capacity for a development.
